sentences.text: POINTS FOR DETERMINATION 7.1
I have considered the arguments of the parties and have perused the record.

7.2 The relevant provisions applicable in present case are reproduced herewith:-
Section 498A IPC provides - "Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished FIR No.
351/2014 State v. Manoj Kumar Page no. 14 of 24 with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine."
Explanation:- For the purpose of this section, "cruelty" means- (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.
Section 304B IPC provides - (1) "Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called "dowry death", and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death".

(2) "Whoever commits dowry death shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to imprisonment for life".
7.3

Thus, after considering the facts of the case and the arguments of FIR No. 351/2014 State v.
Manoj Kumar Page no. 15 of 24 the parties, following points for determination arise: -
1.
Whether the testimony of complainant is credible?
2. Whether all the ingredients of Section 498A and 304B are proved against the accused?
3. Whether the accused is liable to be convicted for any of the alleged offences?

8. APPRECIATION OF EVIDENCE AND APPLICATION OF LAW 8.1 Scrutiny of testimony of complainant:

sentences.text: The main witness of the case is the complainant/PW-1 Panna Lal.
Thus, the case of prosecution depends on his credibility.
Let us proceed further to analyze his testimony.
8.1 (a) Lack of corroboration regarding principal facts.
PW1 Panna Lal has deposed that after about 1 year of the marriage the accused persons demanded Rs.4 lakhs and that they used to harass and beat his daughter.

However, neither any specific date,
month, location or any occasion is mentioned when such demand was so raised.

The brother of the complainant i.e. PW-2 Chhote Lal has deposed that after sometime of the marriage, his brother Panna Lal and niece Saraswati told him that accused Manoj, his parents and his sisters were harassing Saraswati for bringing more money from his brother Panna Lal.
However, he has nowhere mentioned the specific demand of Rs.4 lakh.
Further, nephew of complainant i.e. PW-3 Sharad FIR No. 351/2014 State v. Manoj Kumar Page no. 16 of 24 Chand has not even mentioned about such demand of Rs.4 lakh or other dowry demand.

entities.text: State v. Manoj Kumar Page no. 16 of 24
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He has only deposed that accused Manoj used to harass and beat his sister Nikki and that the mother of accused Manoj never used to allow her at her matrimonial home.

In normal circumstances, if PW-1 was facing dowry demands from the in-laws of his daughter and was unable to meet the same and even his daughter was being harassed on account of such demand, in all likelihood he would have shared his predicament with his other family members i.e. his real brother/PW-2 Chhote Lal and his nephew PW-3 Sharad Chand.
However, the non-mentioning of such demands by these witnesses discredit the testimony of complainant regarding the alleged demand.
8.1 (b) Falsity of allegations against co-accused and resultant diminished credibility of the allegations:

Further, PW-1 Panna Lal has deposed that when he expressed his inability to arrange Rs.4 lakh then the mother-in-law, father-in-law, bua, fufa, sisters-in-law Aarti, Bharti and Jyoti started harassing his daughter and they used to beat her.
It may be noted that PW-3 Sharad Chand has not mentioned the role of said persons in harassment/beatings of his cousin Nikki.
Moreover, as per the charge-sheet itself, the bua and fufa of accused Manoj were issueless and the fufa Munna Lal was deaf and had renal failure and had to undergo the dialysis every week.
As per charge-sheet during local enquiry it was found that the disputes between accused Manoj and his wife Nikki were regarding the unemployment of accused.

Further, as per charge-sheet the IO also believed the FIR No. 351/2014 State v. Manoj Kumar Page no. 17 of 24 version of the other family members who stated that the deceased visited only twice at village Rajeypur, Kanpur and Kishanganj, Delhi to meet them and that she used to reside at her parents' house most of the times.
Therefore, it appears that even IO did not find substance in the allegations against the other family members and regarding the nature of quarrel between deceased and accused.
Accordingly, the allegations of the complainant are not supported by investigation in their entirety.
Moreover, during his cross-examination PW-1 Panna Lal admitted that after marriage his daughter stayed at her parental home most of the time.

Even PW3 Sharad Chand has deposed in his cross-examination " during her matrimonial period,

8.1 (c) Deviation of the allegations from normal human conduct:
Further, in his cross-examination PW-1 Panna Lal has deposed that there was no demand of Rs.4 lakh at the time of engagement or before the engagement.

He also deposed that his daughter returned to his house after 6 months of her marriage and lived with them for about 5 months and during said FIR No. 351/2014 State v. Manoj Kumar Page no. 18 of 24 period she did not complain about the misbehavior or dowry demand by her husband/his parents.
Accordingly, by normal human conduct it appears surprising as to how suddenly a huge dowry demand was raised when no demand was raised prior to the marriage or soon after the marriage.

8.1 (d)
Improvements/variations in the statement of complainant:
During his cross-examination PW-1 Panna Lal also deposed that when he had confronted accused Manoj Kumar as to why he and his parents were harassing Nikki for bringing Rs.4 lakhs, Manoj Kumar replied that he was not demanding the same but his parents are demanding the amount.

PW-1 further deposed that his daughter refused to return with her husband and the accused brought some of his relatives to show PW-1 that accused and his parents will not harass his daughter in future for dowry demand.
However, no such sequence of facts have been mentioned in the statement given by complainant to SDM.
Moreover, during his cross-

PW-1 deposed that he does not know the names of those relatives.
Further, in his cross-examination PW-1 Panna Lal also deposed that accused neither demanded Rs.4 lakhs from him nor from his wife directly but he used to demand the same through his daughter.
However, no such fact has been mentioned in the statement to the SDM.
Rather, as per statement Ex.PW1/A the allegations are regarding the direct demand by in-laws.
8.1 (e) Admitted incomplete information with complainant:

It may also be noted that during his cross-examination PW1 Panna FIR No. 351/2014 State v. Manoj Kumar Page no. 19 of 24 Lal also deposed that Nikki also told him that there are some facts which she will tell to her mother only and he does not know what private matters she disclosed to her mother.
He also admitted till today he was not aware about those private matters as even his wife did not tell him regarding the same.
Thus, admittedly, the deceased did not share all the details about her matrimonial life with PW-1.

Moreover, the wife of PW-1 has not been cited as a witness to bring the complete facts before the Court regarding the matrimonial life of State vs Manoj Kumar Etc on 4 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186948392/

During his cross- examination PW1 also admitted that after 1 year of the marriage of his daughter he came to know about the defect in the hand of accused Manoj.
He admitted that his daughter was upset on this issue of defect in the hand of accused Manoj.
He further deposed that after coming to know about this, he went to house of Manoj where his daughter told him that due to this defect Manoj could not do work properly for earning his livelihood.
It may be reiterated that as per charge- sheet in the local enquiry it was found that the quarrels between accused and deceased were on account of the unemployment of accused Manoj.
Therefore, considering the said statement of PW1 the said cause regarding quarrels cannot be ruled out (instead of quarrels being related to dowry demand/harassment).
8.1 (f) Alleged documents executed by complainant regarding innocence of accused:
Further, during his cross-examination PW1 Panna Lal admitted his signatures on document Mark PW1/DX.

Said document is a copy of affidavit FIR No. 351/2014 State v. Manoj Kumar Page no. 20 of 24 mentioning Panna Lal as deponent and it is mentioned in Para 4 therein " that I have also verified the circumstances of suicide committed my daughter and I am satisfied that none of the accused persons were responsible for that suicide as my daughter was under tension after the suicide committed by my younger daughter Shashi".

Further, in Para 5 of said document it is also mentioned " that I never meant to prosecute any of the accused persons for any act which they have not committed and my statement recorded by the Ld. SDM be either corrected or recorded afresh".
It may be noted that PW1 admitted his signature on the said document but did not offer any explanation regarding the document or contents thereof.

Moreover, another settlement in original i.e. Ex.PW1/DX1 was also put to PW1 during his cross-examination and he admitted that the custody of the daughter of deceased and Manoj was settled to be with her grand parents vide said settlement deed bearing his signatures at point A.

It may be noted that the settlement deed has been notarized on 20.06.2014 and even copy of affidavit Mark PW1/DX was also apparently attested by Oath Commissioner on 20.06.2014.Therefore, it appears that the affidavit Mark PW1/DX was also executed by PW1.
Since said affidavit absolves all the accused, therefore, the allegations of the complainant do not inspire confidence against accused Manoj also.

8.1 (g) Exculpatory facts stated by other prosecution witnesses:
During his cross-examination PW3 Sharad Chand deposed that the deceased Nikki never told him that either her husband accused Manoj or any FIR No. 351/2014 State v. Manoj Kumar Page no. 21 of 24 member of her in-laws family had ever abused or harassed her.

Further, the neighbors residing near the spot of incident i.e. PW-4 Mukesh Babu and PW-5 Shanti Devi have deposed that Manoj and Nikki were having good relations and denied that there used to be frequent fights/quarrels between them.

8.2 No other evidence regarding the allegations:
State vs Manoj Kumar Etc on 4 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186948392/
11
Besides the complainant, PW2 Chhote Lal has also deposed about dowry demands but as mentioned earlier he has not mentioned about any specific demand.

Further,
such demands were not made in the presence of PW2.

Rather, as per his testimony,
he learnt about said demands from PW1 and the deceased.
The facts, if any, told by PW1 to PW2 shall fall under the category of hearsay evidence only and are therefore irrelevant.
As far as the facts, if any, stated by deceased to PW2 are concerned, no specific date, month or any occasion has been mentioned when he got to know such facts from deceased.
Rather, in his cross-examination he has deposed that he never met deceased at her matrimonial house.
He deposed that he met the deceased at her matrimonial house twice or thrice.
Initially, she was happy when she met him but later on she was not ready to accompany the accused to Delhi as she was not getting proper food by the accused.
Thus, he has attributed a different reason for the refusal of deceased to accompany the deceased to her matrimonial house.
Thus, even the testimony of PW2 is not much credible regarding dowry demands and consequent harassment due to non-fulfillment of such demands.

As far PW3 Sharad Chand is concerned, though he has made FIR No. 351/2014 State v. Manoj Kumar Page no. 22 of 24 allegations of harassment/beating of deceased by accused Manoj but neither he has mentioned that he was witness to such harassment/beatings nor he has mentioned the source of his information about the same.
During his cross- examination, he deposed that his brother-in-law had told him about the said harassment to Nikki on 12.06.2014.
Therefore, even his testimony is apparently hearsay and therefore irrelevant for the Court.
Further, in his cross-examination he has also deposed that the deceased Nikki never told him that either her husband Manoj or any member of her in-laws family had ever abused or harassed her.
He also admitted that he visited the in-laws of his cousin sister Nikki but he never discussed the issue of harassment.
He also deposed in his cross-examination that he himself did not go to the in-laws house of Nikki to know about the harassment and for making such complaints.
Hence, neither testimony of PW2 nor PW3 is sufficient to prove the allegations.

8.3 Lack of proof of all the ingredients of alleged offences:
Therefore, even though the marriage of accused and deceased is not disputed and the unnatural death within 7 years of marriage has also been proved but the dowry demands/consequent harassment has not been proved by the prosecution beyond unreasonable doubts.
Accordingly, neither the ingredients of Section 498A nor ingredients of Section 304B IPC have been proved by prosecution.
FIR No. 351/2014 State v. Manoj Kumar Page no. 23 of 24 9. CONCLUSION 9.1
In view of above said discussion, none of the points for determination can be decided in favor of prosecution.
Accordingly, accused Manoj Kumar is acquitted from all the offences charged against him.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
7.2 The relevant provisions applicable in present case are reproduced herewith:-
Section 498A IPC provides - "Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished FIR No.
351/2014 State v. Manoj Kumar Page no. 14 of 24 with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine."
Explanation:- For the purpose of this section, "cruelty" means- (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.
Section 304B IPC provides - (1) "Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called "dowry death", and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death".
(2) "Whoever commits dowry death shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to imprisonment for life".
